purpose: Teach: 美少女/パラダイス/ウォーキング/トリオ/バーベキュー/ボイス/バンクーバー/愛車

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが「美少女」アニメに驚かれたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he used to be quite taken aback by those beauty anime.
lines.style: Gentle, nostalgic opening. Soft voice like reaching back through time. Slow, deliberate pacing. Almost wondering aloud—checking the memory as he speaks it.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃんはハワイをパラダイスと呼んでらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, your grandfather used to call Hawaii his paradise, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm, conversational lilt. A slight turn upward at the end—genuine question with gentle knowingness underneath. Steady pace, comfortable pauses.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが毎朝ウォーキングされたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he went walking every single morning.
lines.style: Quiet, admiring tone. Deliberate on the 'every morning'—small respect for the discipline. Distant gaze in the voice, like watching the memory unfold.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃんがトリオで合唱を楽しまれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather loved singing in that trio choir, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Bright but controlled warmth. A smile in the voice. Ending with genuine affection in 'dear'—acknowledging she's speaking to someone she's chosen to remember with.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがバーベキューをよくされたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he loved grilling—barbecues all the time.
lines.style: Soft, almost fond observation. Steady pace through the line. A small warmth on 'loved grilling'—not forced, just honest recollection.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ラジオ放送のボイスをお気に入りでしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather had such a soft spot for that radio broadcaster's voice, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Conversational and knowing. A slight conspiratorial gentleness—two people remembering the same thing. Warm ending on 'dear', like confirming a shared truth.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがバンクーバーのお話されたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he used to tell stories about Vancouver.
lines.style: Soft, reaching back into time. The word 'Vancouver' carries a little wistfulness—a place that meant something. Slow, like turning pages in memory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ご自身の愛車をいつも磨かれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather always kept his car so polished—his pride and joy, wasn't it, dear?
lines.style: Warm, affectionate chuckle underneath the words. A little knowing—tender nostalgia for a man's simple devotion. Gentle tease in 'pride and joy', ending with genuine warmth.
